source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Prime DFW01-01 publishes 20 MW of IT capacity across 213,000 square feet of technical space in Dallas, making it the sixth-largest facility by published capacity in Texas.

At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 20 MW supports roughly 500 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a density typical of mixed colocation, it supports around 2,000 racks. The operator has not disclosed which density the facility is designed for. The facility's power density works out to 94 watts per square foot, consistent with a mixed-use colocation build rather than a purpose-built AI training hall, though the operator has not confirmed this.

SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 certifications indicate the facility can host tenants with data-handling and international security compliance requirements. Both certifications are published. No tenant names are published.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities. Only 13 publish megawatt figures, accounting for 389 MW of published IT capacity in the state. The remaining 120 facilities publish no capacity data, so 389 MW is a floor on true state capacity, not a ceiling. Prime DFW01-01 represents roughly 5 percent of that published total, a meaningful but not dominant share of the visible infrastructure in its region.
